headline: 26 turnovers sink Celtics in one-point loss to Hawks

off.text: Next: Sun, Nov 29 at Spurs, 4:00 PM
Next: Sun, Nov 29 at Chargers, 4:05 PM
Next: Sun, Nov 29 vs Canucks, 5:00 PM

storylines: San Antonio (16–4) leads the West, is 8–1 on the road and 8–3 at home, and has won eight of its last 10.
Boston opens a back-to-back, at Dallas on Monday, after a season-high 26 turnovers against Atlanta.
Mitchell Robinson has missed four straight games with COVID, leaving the middle to Neemias Queta.
celtics.edge: San Antonio on paper: 116.4 points a game to Boston's 110.9 and a +10.8 average margin to Boston's +8.8, though the Celtics allow fewer (102.1 to 105.5).

storylines: Tommy DeVito makes his first Patriots start against DJ Uiagalelei, with Justin Herbert (concussion) ruled out.
Drake Maye, A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Carlton Davis III are out; Alijah Vera-Tucker could be activated from IR by Saturday afternoon.
Los Angeles is 0–5 at home and has been outscored by 98 points; New England has lost two straight.
patriots.edge: New England on paper: 5–5 with a −21 point differential against a 1–9 team at −98 that is now without Herbert.

storylines: David Pastrnak (lower body) left Friday's game in the first period; Marco Sturm said the team would know more Saturday.
Vancouver (6–21–1) has the fewest points in the West, is 4–11–1 on the road and lost 5–2 in Philadelphia on Friday.
Boston has lost two straight and five of its last six at home.
bruins.edge: Boston on paper: 31 points to Vancouver's 13 and 68 goals allowed in 25 games to the Canucks' 124 in 28, with Pastrnak's status the big unknown.

results.headline: 26 turnovers sink Celtics in one-point loss to Hawks
results.takeaway: Boston blew a 15-point third-quarter lead and committed 26 turnovers, the last by Jayson Tatum with 3.8 seconds left, as Atlanta won 87–86. The Celtics still reach the NBA Cup quarterfinals as the East wild card, at Detroit on Dec. 5.

videos.title: Hawks at Celtics: full game highlights

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: Atlanta missed 11 of its first 12 shots, and Jayson Tatum scored 13 in the quarter, capped by a step-back three for a 26–13 lead. Payton Pritchard's step-back three with 29 seconds left made it 29–14.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: Sam Hauser's three and tip-in stretched the lead to 37–20 early in the quarter. Aaron Wiggins and Jalen Johnson kept Atlanta within reach as Paul George committed four turnovers in the quarter, and Hugo Gonzalez's floater made it 51–39 at the half.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: George hit two threes and Neemias Queta's layup made it 65–50 with 6:26 left. Atlanta closed on a 20–4 run, with threes from Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Luguentz Dort, Johnson and Wiggins, and Dyson Daniels' floater with 11.5 seconds left gave the Hawks their first lead, 70–69.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Hauser's three put Boston up 78–77 with 7:48 left, its last lead, and the Celtics then went 5:32 without a point as Atlanta went ahead 81–78. Derrick White's floater tied it 83–83 with 1:10 left, Alexander-Walker answered with a driving layup at 54.3 seconds, and after Tatum stole the ball back he threw it away with 3.8 seconds left. White's three at the buzzer made the final 87–86.

performers.name: Neemias Queta
performers.note: Grabbed a career-high 22 rebounds starting in place of Mitchell Robinson, but also had a team-high seven turnovers.

performers.name: Jayson Tatum
performers.note: Scored 13 in the first quarter and none in the fourth, and his turnover with 3.8 seconds left ended Boston's last chance.

performers.name: Derrick White
performers.note: Scored Boston's last seven points, including the tying floater with 1:10 left and a three at the buzzer.

results.oppLine: Jalen Johnson had 24 points and 12 rebounds; Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 20, including Atlanta's last four, and Luguentz Dort added 14 off the bench.

results.headline: Rielly's two goals sink Bruins, who lose Pastrnak
results.takeaway: Morgan Rielly scored twice, the go-ahead goal off a faceoff with 2:04 left in the second, and Toronto beat Boston 3–1. David Pastrnak, the team's leading scorer, left in the first period with a lower-body injury and did not return.

videos.title: Maple Leafs at Bruins: full game highlights

sections.label: 1st period
sections.text: Casey Mittelstadt scored on the power play at 6:31, from Mason Lohrei and JJ Peterka, for a 1–0 lead. David Pastrnak left the bench with about six minutes left in the period, and the Bruins announced a lower-body injury before the second. Morgan Rielly's wrist shot from the point, through traffic in front of Jeremy Swayman, tied it 1–1 at 16:53.

sections.label: 2nd period
sections.text: Toronto lost defenseman Chris Tanev to a lower-body injury after a collision with Mark Kastelic three minutes in. Rielly scored again off a faceoff win in Boston's zone with 2:04 left, the 100th goal of his career, for a 2–1 lead.

sections.label: 3rd period
sections.text: Boston got one shot on a 5-on-3 that lasted 1:58 early in the period. Colton Sissons made it 3–1 at 7:24, from Gavin McKenna, and Anthony Stolarz shut the door the rest of the way.

performers.name: Casey Mittelstadt
performers.note: Scored Boston's only goal, his ninth, on the power play.

performers.name: JJ Peterka
performers.note: Led the Bruins with five shots and set up Mittelstadt's goal.

performers.name: Jeremy Swayman
performers.note: Toronto scored three times on 18 shots, including Rielly's long-range equalizer through traffic.

results.oppLine: Morgan Rielly scored his first two goals of the season; Colton Sissons had a goal and an assist, and Anthony Stolarz made 28 saves.

bruins.headline: Pastrnak leaves with lower-body injury
bruins.summary: David Pastrnak left Friday's game in the first period with a lower-body injury and did not return. "It was a lower-body injury. He's being tested right now. We'll probably know more tomorrow," Marco Sturm said. Pastrnak leads Boston with 32 points (11 goals, 21 assists) in 24 games.

bruins.headline: Five losses in six home games
bruins.summary: Friday's loss was Boston's fifth in its last six home games. The Bruins host Vancouver on Sunday in the fourth game of a six-game homestand.

bruins.headline: Sturm: top line's start was 'disrespectful'
bruins.summary: Marco Sturm faulted Geekie, Lindholm and Pastrnak for giving up a rush goal on the first shift against Winnipeg's top line. "This is disrespectful, I thought, versus a line who's been probably the hottest line in hockey right now," he said. All three finished minus-4.

bruins.headline: Hagens back at practice
bruins.summary: James Hagens, out since a cross-check against Pittsburgh on Nov. 5, practiced Tuesday in a non-contact jersey. "This is the next block," Marco Sturm said; neither he nor Hagens gave a return date. Hagens has 12 points in 17 games.

bruins.headline: Geekie leads the team in power-play goals
bruins.summary: Morgan Geekie's power-play goal against Winnipeg, off a cross-ice feed from David Pastrnak, was his fourth with the man advantage, the most on the team. Jeremy Swayman said Boston needed to be ready from the opening puck drop.

bruins.headline: McAvoy back on the pie route
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy resumed the Bruins' Thanksgiving pie delivery, a team tradition since 2009, after missing last year's with a broken jaw. He delivered to St. Francis House and Pine Street Inn and said he was thankful to be healthy.

bruins.headline: Khusnutdinov moves up; Geekie drops
bruins.summary: Sturm put Marat Khusnutdinov on the top line for the third period, moving Geekie to the third line. He said it wasn't a message about Geekie's turnover: "They needed help... I thought [Khusnutdinov] did a good job and stabilized that line."

bruins.headline: Jeannot's fight with Bauer
bruins.summary: Tanner Jeannot fought Tyrel Bauer, who leads the NHL with five fights, for about a minute at center ice. It was Jeannot's fourth fight of the season and 12th as a Bruin. "He's the heart and soul of this team," Jeremy Swayman said.

bruins.headline: Lindholm's first four-goal game
bruins.summary: Elias Lindholm scored four times against Washington, his first four-goal game and first hat trick as a Bruin. He is tied with David Pastrnak for the team lead with 11 goals.

celtics.headline: Cup quarterfinal at Detroit on Dec. 5
celtics.summary: Boston advanced to the NBA Cup quarterfinals as the Eastern Conference wild card and will play at Detroit, the Group A winner, at 7:30 p.m. on Saturday, Dec. 5. Atlanta won Group C on the head-to-head result after both teams finished 3–1. It is Boston's first quarterfinal in three years.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla: 'That was on me'
celtics.summary: Joe Mazzulla took the blame for Boston's second-half offense against Atlanta: "Our play calling wasn't right. We didn't put them in position to make the right read. That was on me." The Celtics scored fewer than 100 points for the third time in four games.

celtics.headline: Robinson's absence was COVID
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson's four-game absence has been due to COVID, Joe Mazzulla said Friday. Neemias Queta started again at center and had a career-high 22 rebounds against Atlanta.

celtics.headline: Most turnovers of the Mazzulla era
celtics.summary: Boston's 26 turnovers against Atlanta were the most ever by a Joe Mazzulla-coached Celtics team. Neemias Queta had seven, Paul George six and Jayson Tatum four.

celtics.headline: Tatum on the final steal: 'You should never assume'
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum stole the ball with 9.1 seconds left and Boston down two, then passed on a timeout and threw it away. "I thought I got fouled, didn't call it, and turned the ball over," he said. "You should never assume, especially in those moments." He is averaging 4 points in fourth quarters this season.

celtics.headline: Tatum's biggest night since the Achilles
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum's 41 points were his most since 46 against Cleveland on Feb. 28, 2025, and his 31st career 40-point game. "We had a tough last week, for various reasons," he said. "We can't change what happened; we can only focus on today."

celtics.headline: George reaches 2,500 career threes
celtics.summary: Paul George became the eighth player in NBA history to make 2,500 3-pointers, on a 6-of-9 night from deep with 28 points and nine assists. Neemias Queta added a season-high 21 on 9-of-11 shooting.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla ties Phil Jackson to 250 wins
celtics.summary: Joe Mazzulla reached 250 wins in his 346th game, tying Phil Jackson as the second-fastest coach to get there. Only Steve Kerr (302 games) did it faster.

celtics.headline: Scheierman's late eight
celtics.summary: Baylor Scheierman, scoreless for the first 45 and a half minutes, scored eight straight Celtics points in 1:15 after Washington cut a 34-point lead to seven. Boston was playing its third game in four nights.

celtics.headline: Tatum passes Bill Russell
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum's 27 points against the Warriors moved him to 14,528 career points, past Bill Russell (14,522) for eighth on the Celtics' all-time scoring list. Sam Jones is seventh at 15,411.

patriots.headline: Herbert ruled out; DeVito vs. Uiagalelei
patriots.summary: The Chargers ruled out Justin Herbert (concussion), running back Keaton Mitchell and linebacker Daiyan Henley on Friday's final injury report, so Tommy DeVito's first Patriots start comes against DJ Uiagalelei. Akheem Mesidor and Brenen Thompson are doubtful.

patriots.headline: Doubs out, didn't travel
patriots.summary: New England ruled out Drake Maye, A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Carlton Davis III. Doubs, limited in two practices, did not travel and needs at least one more week; Christian Barmore, Reggie Gilliam, Walter Rouse and Alijah Vera-Tucker are questionable.

patriots.headline: Vera-Tucker decision due Saturday
patriots.summary: The Patriots have until 4 p.m. ET Saturday to activate Alijah Vera-Tucker from injured reserve. With him and Ben Brown back, they could start their most-used line: Will Campbell, Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Brown and Morgan Moses, who have played 105 snaps together.

patriots.headline: Maye not on IR, for now
patriots.summary: New England hasn't placed Drake Maye (fibula) on injured reserve. The team has used seven of its eight IR-return designations, so Maye could stay on the 53-man roster to keep a return this season possible.

patriots.headline: Maye out at least six weeks
patriots.summary: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Drake Maye is out at least six weeks with his fractured right fibula. A return this season has not been ruled out.

patriots.headline: Kuhr: 'We got hit in the mouth'
patriots.summary: Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr cited Willie Mays' 1965 MVP season, which included an 0-for-24 stretch, as the approach he wants from his unit. "We got hit in the mouth. Let's regroup," he said.

patriots.headline: Patriots not adding a quarterback
patriots.summary: No team claimed Daniel Jones, and Mike Vrabel said adding a quarterback isn't "something that's going to happen here in the next few days." New England has two healthy QBs and none on the practice squad, and wants the reps to develop rookie Behren Morton.

patriots.headline: Vrabel: 'Tommy's our starter'
patriots.summary: Asked about Jones, Mike Vrabel said "Tommy's our starter." Tommy DeVito went 12-of-24 for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception in relief in Munich and is 3–5 in eight career starts.

redsox.headline: Lockout expected when CBA expires Dec. 1
redsox.summary: MLB's collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and a lockout is widely expected. The deadline has pushed clubs, including the Red Sox, to move quickly this month.

redsox.headline: Oviedo traded to Arizona
redsox.summary: Boston traded right-hander Johan Oviedo to the Diamondbacks for minor league lefty Luke Dotson, 22, and a player to be named later or cash. Oviedo pitched once for Boston, on March 30, before going on the injured list with a right elbow strain.

redsox.headline: Sandoval signs with Colorado
redsox.summary: Left-hander Patrick Sandoval, now a former Red Sox, agreed to a three-year, $42 million deal with the Rockies on Wednesday night, per ESPN's Jeff Passan.

redsox.headline: Gil signs with Detroit
redsox.summary: Luis Gil signed a one-year, $2.3 million deal with the Tigers, per ESPN's Jeff Passan. Boston had interest, per the Globe, but never made an offer, per MassLive.

redsox.headline: Duran and Casas tendered
redsox.summary: Boston tendered all of its remaining arbitration-eligible players at the Nov. 20 deadline, including Jarren Duran (projected $11.1 million) and Triston Casas (projected $1.7 million). None has agreed to terms yet.

redsox.headline: Connor Wong non-tendered
redsox.summary: Catcher Connor Wong, designated for assignment after the Nick Fortes trade, was non-tendered and became a free agent.

redsox.headline: Four bench players avoid arbitration
redsox.summary: Gonzalez, Monasterio, White and Jones signed one-year deals on deadline day.

redsox.headline: Gray: a Red Sox reunion 'never really came up'
redsox.summary: Sonny Gray, who signed with Minnesota, said talks with Boston "never really got close" but that "Boston was great… I loved it there, man. I truly did."

redsox.headline: Fortes to back up Rutschman
redsox.summary: Nick Fortes, acquired from Tampa Bay for 17-year-old right-hander Angel Roa, hit .258 with 6 homers and 35 RBIs in 109 games in 2026. Craig Breslow called him a "really strong defender who has a great reputation in working with a pitching staff." Connor Wong was designated for assignment to make room.

redsox.headline: Breslow: 'I think we have a good lineup'
redsox.summary: With Jake Bauers signed for four years and $58 million, Craig Breslow said, "I think we have a good lineup," and that it's hard to envision something else significant on the horizon. Bauers had a .389 on-base percentage in 2026, third in the majors.

nba.cutNote: Top 6 make the playoffs, 7–10 the play-in

nhl.cutNote: Top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards make the playoffs

nfl.cutNote: Top 7 make the playoffs (division winners seeded 1–4)
